coverage.method: Tests scan TypeScript/JavaScript AST identifier and string-literal names matching EINZBERN_* or TCRN_* in these source roots, including literal names used by computed lookups; browser keys and lifecycle/catalog parser parity have separate checks.

exclusions.reason: OS/runtime and cloud-folder hints or child-environment controls, not owned product configuration. HOME/homedir resolves user home; Windows cloud hints only suggest cloudHosted. Explicit host input CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR/CLAUDE_CODE_EXECPATH is registered separately.

paths: scripts other than listed entry/support files
exclusions.reason: Release/CI/proof/legacy platform maintenance and test-controller controls are separate tool contracts, not ordinary engine or Atelier startup settings. Includes TCRN_BACKUP_*, TCRN_SSH_*, TCRN_DS_*, TCRN_TEST_CONTROLLER_*, EINZBERN_P1_INJECT and EINZBERN_PRIVACY_HISTORY_BASE; no values are read or exported.

Installed current/previous records, receipts, managed-section digests, browser in-memory selection and generated config are state/output, not editable entries. Retired signature trust/archive/SSH control-tree settings are not revived.

Static discovery cannot prove arbitrary computed names, external plugins, shell/OS behavior or real installed host state. New source entrypoints and dynamic name builders require explicit review; this is not a whole-repository getenv exhaustiveness claim.

limits: Metadata never reads process.env, localStorage, host files, credentials or actual runtime values; no runtime behavior or authority changes.

Detailed per-field defaults cover the registered runtime/startup/browser/lifecycle entries, not every operational CLI payload. All supplied command flags retain their original catalog metadata without inferred defaults.
Null defaultValue is not an empty-string default: defaultDescription distinguishes required, absent and contextual defaults. Precedence is consumer-specific.
Discovery is bounded to the declared source roots and explicit entry/support files. Tests detect new literal product-owned names there; dynamic names and excluded tools need separate review.
Presence of a consumer reference proves source wiring only, not real host acceptance, installation state, live quota access or user approval.
Registered settings and runtime inputs have separate ownership contracts; command flag structure comes from the canonical command catalog.
Consumer descriptions identify source wiring, not live-host acceptance or account access.
Readback metadata does not migrate events, refresh projections, or attest installed-version state.
